article.title: Jury Deliberates in Murder Trial of Ex-Cop Matthew Farwell Over Sandra Birchmore's Death
article.summary: A federal jury is now deliberating the fate of former Massachusetts police officer Matthew Farwell, who is accused by prosecutors of murdering 23-year-old Sandra Birchmore and her unborn son in 2021 after years of sexual abuse.

article.content_html:
Key Developments

The fate of former Stoughton, Massachusetts police officer Matthew Farwell is in the hands of a federal jury following closing arguments in U.S. District Court in Boston. Federal prosecutors charged Farwell in 2024 with killing a witness or a victim, alleging he murdered Birchmore to silence her about years of sexual abuse that began when she was 15 and he was 27. In 2025, he was additionally charged with causing the death of an unborn child. Farwell, who pleaded not guilty, did not take the witness stand during the trial. While his defense attorneys did not deny that he had an affair with Birchmore, they attempted to cast doubt on the prosecution's theory of the case and the manner of her death.

Key Takeaways

  • Alleged Ultimatum: Text messages revealed during the trial showed Birchmore gave Farwell an ultimatum to impregnate her or face exposure of their affair to his wife.
  • Pregnancy Disclosed: By late December 2020, Birchmore became pregnant and sent Farwell a poster announcing they were going to be parents, prompting hostile text exchanges.
  • Investigation Shift: Birchmore's manner of death was initially ruled a suicide by local authorities before being changed to undetermined, eventually triggering a federal investigation and subsequent charges.

Why It Matters

The case has drawn widespread attention due to the severe allegations of abuse of power by a law enforcement officer involved in a youth outreach program. The trial highlights critical issues surrounding institutional accountability, the handling of initial death investigations involving vulnerable victims, and federal prosecution of crimes allegedly committed to silence witnesses.
